title: Introduce RBACv2 migration toolchain, region-pinned KMS enforcement, and deterministic audit IDs
author: Marina Patel
description: Motivation: customers and internal security reviews highlighted two operational gaps: (1) inconsistent behavior when a service scoped RBACv2 policy referenced KMS keys in multiple regions (we need a deterministic enforcement mode for 'region pin' to avoid silent cross-region key usage), and (2) audit log entries for policy evaluation used non-deterministic IDs which made forensic replays and test harness comparisons brittle. This PR introduces a migration toolchain for RBACv2 policy templates, a conservative opt-in region-pinned KMS enforcement mode, and deterministic audit ID generation. Summary of changes: (a) migration tool: tooling/rbacv2/migrate_policy_templates.py - a CLI that validates legacy role bindings, emits a proposed RBACv2 manifest, and can apply a dry-run diff to a target namespace; it includes a --conservative flag that preserves implicit operator roles to reduce blast radius. (b) region-pinned KMS enforcement: auth/kms/region_pin_enforcer.go and config schema changes (api/v1/security.yaml) add enforcement.mode = [off|warn|enforce] and enforcement.kms_region_preference list. When set to 'enforce' the runtime rejects requests that attempt to use a KMS key outside the declared pinned regions; 'warn' logs an audit event and allows fallthrough to compatible local key variants. (c) audit: internal/audit/deterministic_ids.go replaces timestamp/random UUID mixing with a deterministic ID derived from sha256(namespace + request_id + policy_fingerprint) encoded as base62, ensuring stable IDs for identical evaluation traces (useful for tests and replays). (d) tests and dashboards: added unit + integration tests (tests/rbacv2/*, tests/integration/kms_region_pin) and a Grafana dashboard tile that surfaces 'kms_region_mismatch' audit count. Rollout plan and feature flags: region-pinned behavior is behind a feature flag security.region_pin.enforcement which defaults to off in main. Migration tool produces a Linear export and a suggested canary set of namespaces to opt into 'warn' first. We performed a staged rollout: opt-in with two internal tenants for 48h, observed no rejects, then switched those to 'enforce' with automatic fallback to region-local surrogate keys for specific legacy services. Safety and rollback: the enforcer records an audit event with action=reject/warn and includes the deterministic audit ID; operators can toggle enforcement.mode to off to immediately revert. For migrations that touch many bindings the CLI supports --batch-size and a dry-run CSV export to review. Backwards compatibility notes: when enforcement.mode is off we do not change runtime behavior. Migration tool will not auto-mutate production policies without explicit --apply. Testing and CI: initial CI run failed linting (go vet) on kms enforcer comment formatting; fixed in commit 0002. Integration test harness includes a synthetic KMS provider that simulates cross-region errors and validates that the enforcer surfaces consistent audit entries. Security review: SEC-204 requested explicit audit of fallback paths; added logs and a small counter metric (security_kms_pin_fallback_total). Observability: added tracing spans for policy evaluation fingerprinting and a per-request tag for pinned_region. Documentation: docs/security/rbacv2_migration.md and a short runbook for operators in docs/runbooks/kms_region_pin.md. See release notes for admin guidance.
commits: 1) 0001/initial: add migration CLI, kms enforcer skeleton, deterministic audit id implementation (migrate_policy_templates.py, region_pin_enforcer.go, deterministic_ids.go, api/v1/security.yaml). 2) 0002/fix-lint: address go vet/lint feedback and add comments. 3) 0003/tests: add unit and integration tests + synthetic kms provider. 4) 0004/docs: operator docs and runbook.
discussion:
Reviewer Alice Kim: 'Overall this looks good; two asks: a) can we provide a migration dry-run JSON output that includes suggested enforcement.mode per-namespace based on historical KMS usage? b) please add a short explanation why we use base62 for audit IDs instead of hex.'
Author Marina: 'a) added --export-json in 0001 that emits per-namespace suggestions using a simple heuristic (>=95% single-region usage -> suggest enforce). b) base62 reduces length and is URL-safe without punctuation; added comment and link to RFC in deterministic_ids.go.'
Reviewer Diego Morales: 'Can we avoid a hard reject for services that declare multiple allowed regions but reference a single-key tied to a different region? Suggest warn+metric first.'
Author Marina: 'Agreed. Implementation now checks configured allowed_regions and will only reject when enforcement.mode=enforce and request_key_region not in allowed_regions; otherwise it emits a kms_region_mismatch audit event and increments security_kms_pin_fallback_total. Added integration test to cover this case.'
Reviewer Ravi Shah: 'CI failed earlier; ensure go vet & lint are green and add a short performance note: enforcer should be O(1) per request aside from fingerprint calc.'
Author Marina: 'Addressed linting, and added documentation on expected CPU cost (<0.5% p95 request CPU on busiest path) backed by microbenchmarks in tests/integration. CI green after 0002.'
Approvals: Alice Kim (approved), Diego Morales (approved with one comment addressed), Ravi Shah (LGTM).
release_notes:
- Add RBACv2 migration CLI to generate and validate v2 templates and produce an opt-in enforcement suggestion per namespace.
- Introduce region-pinned KMS enforcement (off|warn|enforce) with safe rollout guidance and a runbook.
- Deterministic audit IDs for policy evaluation traces to improve replayability and forensic matching.
- New metrics: security_kms_pin_fallback_total, and audit events for kms_region_mismatch.
Operators: enable security.region_pin.enforcement=warn before enforce and use the migration CLI --export-json to verify suggested targets.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps enforcement behind a feature flag. The migration CLI is written to be conservative by default (no auto-apply). We coordinated with SRE to schedule canaries and alert rules before wide rollout.
